vectors.name: plain
vectors.why: A signed envelope verifies, and its ID is the hash of the payload bytes.

vectors.name: unicode_body
vectors.why: Bodies are text, and the ID hashes the bytes as sent.

vectors.name: high_s_signature
vectors.why: Some hardware won't normalize signatures, so both forms verify. The ID ignores the signature, so altering one can't make a replay look new.

vectors.name: low_s_signature
vectors.why: The other form of the same signature, with the same ID.

vectors.name: longest_lifetime
vectors.why: Exactly 30 days is allowed.

vectors.name: clock_tolerance_edge
vectors.why: A sender's clock can run 120 seconds ahead.

vectors.name: last_valid_second
vectors.why: Valid until the second before it expires.

vectors.name: swapped_payload
vectors.why: A signature only fits its own payload.

vectors.name: signed_by_another_key
vectors.why: Mallory signs while claiming to be Ana, checked against Ana.

vectors.name: sender_field_lies
vectors.why: Mallory signs and claims to be Ana, checked against Mallory's real identity.

vectors.name: alg_none
vectors.why: The header can't choose the algorithm.

vectors.name: alg_hs256
vectors.why: The header can't choose the algorithm.

vectors.name: alg_es384
vectors.why: The header can't choose the algorithm.

vectors.name: typ_of_another_object
vectors.why: A signature made for another object type can't be replayed as an envelope.

vectors.name: extra_header_field
vectors.why: Header fields are exact, so no key ID or algorithm hint can steer the check.

vectors.name: duplicate_header_field
vectors.why: Duplicate fields are refused, whichever a parser would keep.

vectors.name: unknown_payload_field
vectors.why: A limit an old verifier ignored would be a hole, so unknown fields are refused.

vectors.name: duplicate_payload_field
vectors.why: One parser might read Ana as the sender and another Mallory.

vectors.name: unknown_version
vectors.why: An unknown version is refused.

vectors.name: float_date
vectors.why: Dates are whole numbers.

vectors.name: negative_date
vectors.why: Dates can't be negative.

vectors.name: payload_not_json
vectors.why: Signed garbage is still garbage.

vectors.name: expired
vectors.why: A message stops at its expiry.

vectors.name: from_the_future
vectors.why: Past the clock tolerance.

vectors.name: lifetime_too_long
vectors.why: Hosts remember a message until it expires, so the lifetime is capped.

vectors.name: padded_payload
vectors.why: Spare bytes would be a channel for a stolen key, and would give one message many IDs.

vectors.name: reordered_payload
vectors.why: So would another field order.

vectors.name: reordered_header
vectors.why: The header is exact, so its bytes can't vary either.

vectors.name: header_with_spaces
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: nonce_too_long
vectors.why: A nonce is 16 bytes, so it can't carry more.

vectors.name: nonce_as_text
vectors.why: An instruction can't live in the nonce.

vectors.name: empty_nonce
vectors.why: A request step has none, since prev already prevents replay.

vectors.name: recipient_not_an_id
vectors.why: A recipient is an ID, not a place for text.

vectors.name: expires_the_moment_it_was_created
vectors.why: A message needs some life, so the dates can't be equal either.

vectors.name: expires_before_it_was_created
vectors.why: A message that ended before it began has no meaning, and nothing should deliver it.

vectors.name: zero_signature
vectors.why: An all-zero signature has passed some broken verifiers.

vectors.name: r_equal_to_order
vectors.why: r and s must be below the curve order.

vectors.name: short_signature
vectors.why: A signature is exactly 64 bytes.

vectors.name: der_signature
vectors.why: Only r and s side by side, not DER.

vectors.name: base64_padding
vectors.why: Base64url here has no padding.

vectors.name: extra_segment
vectors.why: Exactly three parts.

vectors.name: two_segments
vectors.why: Exactly three parts.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.why: Nothing is refused, without a crash.

vectors.name: key_off_the_curve
vectors.why: Some libraries crash on a point that isn't on the curve. It must simply fail.
